package_info.package_manager: Windows (malicious dropper distributed via phishing archive)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is a multi-stage dropper that uses social engineering, sideloading, and obfuscated code to download and execute additional payloads, ultimately enabling remote code execution and further malware deployment on the victim's system.

execution_context.file_location: !PENTING_LIST OF OFFICERS.rar / 062023_PENTING_LIST OF SUPERVISORY OFFICERS WHO STILL HAVE NOT REPORT.pdf.exe

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Executable masquerading as a PDF: 062023_PENTING_LIST OF SUPERVISORY OFFICERS WHO STILL HAVE NOT REPORT.pdf.exe
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user double-clicks the file, the executable runs, drops multiple files (including decoys and malware components), and initiates the infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: A file with a double extension (.pdf.exe) is designed to trick users into thinking it is a document, not an executable.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal PDF files do not execute code or drop additional files; this file abuses user trust and Windows' hidden extensions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; legitimate software does not use double extensions to disguise executables.
key_indicators: Large file size for a supposed document

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: IC.exe reaches out to http://185.225.68.37/jay/nl/VCRUNTIME140_1.dll to download a DLL.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code downloads a malicious DLL from a remote server and saves it locally for later sideloading.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: IC.exe's sole purpose is to download a DLL from an external, non-Microsoft server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not download DLLs from untrusted sources at runtime.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters may download updates, but not DLLs from suspicious servers.
key_indicators: Download of DLL to local system

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Drop and open decoy document: Microsoft Office.doc
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the dropper creates and opens a decoy document to distract the user while malware executes in the background.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dropping and opening a decoy document is a common social engineering tactic to distract users.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers do not open unrelated documents as part of their process.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some installers may show EULAs or documentation, but not as a decoy for malicious activity.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: power.exe decodes and processes obfuscated power.xml, launching seAgnt.exe as specified in the XML Actions tag.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, power.exe reads and decodes an obfuscated XML file, then executes a command to launch seAgnt.exe, continuing the infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated configuration files and automated execution of additional binaries are hallmarks of malware staging.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not use obfuscated XML to hide execution instructions for further binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise software uses XML configs, but not obfuscated or for launching unrelated binaries.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when seAgnt.exe is launched by power.exe)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: seAgnt.exe (renamed GameBarFTServer.exe) loads VCRUNTIME140_1.dll via DLL sideloading.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, a legitimate Microsoft binary is used to sideload a malicious DLL, enabling execution of attacker-controlled code in a trusted process context.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: DLL sideloading is a well-known technique for executing malicious code under the guise of a trusted process.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate binaries should only load trusted, signed DLLs from official sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; sideloading is almost exclusively abused for malicious purposes.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when VCRUNTIME140_1.dll is loaded by seAgnt.exe)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious VCRUNTIME140_1.dll reaches out to http://185.225.68.37/jay/nl/35g3498734gkb.dat to download additional payload.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When loaded, the DLL connects to a remote C2 server to download another file (which is itself a copy of the DLL), enabling further payload delivery or persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: A DLL making outbound network connections to download further payloads is highly indicative of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate runtime DLLs do not perform network operations or self-update from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; system DLLs should not perform these actions.

attack_chain.action: User opens phishing archive and executes disguised dropper executable.
Dropper deploys decoy document, IC.exe, power.exe, power.xml, and seAgnt.exe; opens decoy to distract user.
IC.exe downloads malicious VCRUNTIME140_1.dll from remote server.
power.exe decodes obfuscated power.xml and launches seAgnt.exe.
VCRUNTIME140_1.dll connects to C2 and downloads additional payload (35g3498734gkb.dat).

behavioral_signatures: Execution of files with double extensions (e.g., .pdf.exe)
Dropping and execution of multiple binaries from a single user action
Obfuscated configuration files (e.g., XML with garbage characters)
DLL sideloading via renamed legitimate binaries
Outbound network connections from DLLs to hardcoded IPs/domains
file_indicators: 062023_PENTING_LIST OF SUPERVISORY OFFICERS WHO STILL HAVE NOT REPORT.pdf.exe
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of files with double extensions and unexpected process creation chains involving decoy documents and multiple executables. Detect DLL sideloading by monitoring legitimate binaries (e.g., GameBarFTServer.exe) loading unsigned or suspicious DLLs from non-standard directories. Flag outbound network connections from DLLs or binaries to known malicious IPs/domains. Alert on the presence or execution of the listed file indicators, especially in unusual directories such as ProgramData or AppData.
